title: a header length taken from the stream was used without checking the bytes actually left
object: the packet's bytestream buffer, one direct allocation
lifetime_ender: NONE -- the buffer is alive throughout. SPATIAL row.
shape: a stream-supplied header length is consumed without checking the remaining bytes
allocator_layer: the platform allocator itself: one direct allocation holding the packet, no inner layer.
fidelity: model consumer, real guard. The pre-fix guard checked only header_len's LOWER bound; the case asserts that the declared length exceeds what the buffer holds.
live_proof: absent at the pin: n9.0.1:libavcodec/prores_raw.c carries the two-sided guard `if (header_len < 62 || bytestream2_get_bytes_left(&gb) < header_len - 2)`. The pre-fix form, `if (header_len < 62)`, is at 041d4f010e^ and is absent from the pin. A fix-reversal.

spatial.oracle: PREDICTED, not measured: added after this corpus's last platform run. The crossing leaves a direct allocation, so a per-allocation bound SHOULD fault. On CheriBSD that is conditional on the usable size for this request -- a size class is a step function and the capability length must be read in-guest before the arm is called either way.

cheribsd-revocation.target: stock CheriBSD purecap with libc revocation on
cheribsd-revocation.oracle: MEASURED 2026-10-08, results/2026-10-08-cheribsd/: **CAUGHT.** signal=34, si_code=1 (the BOUNDS code), fault at 0x102240, with supervise resolving `expect ffh_read_probe_u8 0x102230` from the ELF independently of the run -- the fault lies inside the probe's extent, the offset being the -O0 frame setup, and the RANGE is the attribution criterion rather than equality with the symbol address. The crossing leaves the allocator's USABLE size, which is what malloc bounds the capability to, so there is no size-class slack for it to hide in. tools/size-class-audit.py predicted this reading from the measured request size alone, and the two agree.
cheribsd-revocation.platform: stock CheriBSD purecap, kernel CHERI-PURECAP-QEMU, revocation ON (--runtime-revocation on); both platform controls cheribsd-abi and cheribsd-bounds PASSED in the same boot.

native-detect.oracle: the buggy arm's access crosses the allocation and the case's damage flag is set; the fixed arm's bound keeps it inside. The arms differ by the upstream fix, not by protection. status: built 2026-10-08; native arms measured by runners/run-native.sh in the same commit. The platform arms are declared predictions.
nested_why: the crossed buffer is the packet's own allocation, straight from the platform with no inner allocator between, so under the WHO-ALLOCATED axis this row is NOT nested.
distinguishing: the only row here whose crossing length is chosen by the INPUT rather than fixed by the code: header_len comes from the stream, so the overrun is as long as an attacker makes it, and the case caps its own scan so a run cannot wander.
